title: Trait bounds repeated on Verifier struct definition violate Rust API guideline C-STRUCT-BOUNDS
description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:426 declares:

```rust
pub struct Verifier<'a, V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher> {
    anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
    sig_verifier: &'a V,
    rev_checker: &'a R,
    policy: &'a ValidationPolicy,
    aia: &'a A,
}
```

The trait bounds `V: SignatureVerifier`, `R: RevocationChecker`, `A: AiaFetcher` are then repeated verbatim on both impl blocks (lines 434-438, 459-462).

The Rust API Guidelines explicitly recommend against this pattern under [C-STRUCT-BOUNDS](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/future-proofing.html#data-structures-do-not-duplicate-derived-trait-bounds-c-struct-bound):

> Generic type parameters of data structures should not be bound by traits unless the bound is required by the type definition itself.

The bounds on `Verifier` are required by the impl methods that call trait methods on the borrowed values, NOT by the struct itself — the struct could hold `&V: ?Sized` for any `V` and still store it. Storing references to anchors/verifiers/policy does not require any of the trait bounds.

The idiomatic shape is:

```rust
pub struct Verifier<'a, V, R, A = NoAiaFetcher> {
    anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
    sig_verifier: &'a V,
    rev_checker: &'a R,
    policy: &'a ValidationPolicy,
    aia: &'a A,
}

impl<'a, V, R, A> Verifier<'a, V, R, A>
where
    V: SignatureVerifier,
    R: RevocationChecker,
    A: AiaFetcher,
{
    // ...methods that need the bounds...
}
```

What goes wrong if it stays:

1. **Constructor flexibility is artificially constrained.** A caller cannot construct a `Verifier` value at all without satisfying all three bounds, even though the verifier doesn't *use* the bounds until `verify_one` is called. With bounds on impls only, this restriction lifts to the call site where it belongs.

2. **Maintenance burden.** When a new trait method is added to `SignatureVerifier` requiring an additional bound (e.g. `+ Send` for parallel `verify_batch`), the bound must be added in three places (struct + 2 impls) instead of one. Bound drift between the three sites is a real compile-time failure mode.

3. **Reads as "this struct fundamentally requires these traits"** to the reader. It doesn't — only the methods do.

This is one of the most-cited Rust API guideline violations and the fix is mechanical.
close_reason:
Fixed. Verifier is now declared as pub struct Verifier<'a, V, R, A = NoAiaFetcher>.

The bead was correct and the case is the textbook one for C-STRUCT-BOUNDS: every field is a shared reference (&'a V, &'a R, &'a A, &'a [TrustAnchor], &'a ValidationPolicy) plus a Copy AiaConfig, so none of the three traits affects the data representation. Both inherent impls already declared the bounds in their own where clauses, so nothing moved -- the struct-level copies were pure duplication.

Not a breaking change: relaxing a bound only widens what can be named, and callers could never have constructed a non-conforming Verifier anyway since new() requires the traits.

Clone, Copy and Debug dropped the bounds entirely rather than restating them. None needed them: Debug prints the anchor count, policy and config, and copying a bundle of shared references is free whatever they point at.

Side benefit worth noting: this made the existing compile-time assertion strictly stronger. It previously instantiated Verifier over a type implementing the three traits and nothing else -- the most the struct bounds permitted -- and now uses a type implementing NOTHING. One assertion now guards both properties: reinstating a struct bound fails to compile, and replacing the hand-written Clone/Copy with a #[derive] fails too (a derive would add V: Copy bounds the struct does not need, holding &V rather than V).

Verified by mutation: reinstating V: SignatureVerifier on the struct fails the build at the Clone impl with "the trait bound `V: SignatureVerifier` is not satisfied".

Also removed the capability traits from _verifier_is_send_sync, which only ever needed Sync (&T is Send exactly when T is Sync).

Related and still open: PKIX-sqek.19, on whether the three named generics should become a single trust-domain seam. That is an API-shape question and is untouched here -- this change only removes redundancy, it does not alter the parameter list.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2345 tests.
